newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE Brent technicals to lead push higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE Brent technicals to lead push higher.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* August Brent should get through $19 today but some resistance is waiting at $19.06 which represents a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement from the fall that took it from $20.50 to $17.61.
* Gas oil opened and closed at $167.50 a tonne on Wednesday forming a 'Doji at tops' candlestick on the spot month chart which flags uncertainty and indecision by buyers.

Funds short-covering helped set crude prices back into uptrend after a brief dip on Wednesday, but U.S. holidays this weekend could slow momentum and put further gains on hold for a while though technicals remain bullish, analysts said.

"August Brent should get through the $19 today but some resistance is waiting just the other side at $19.06 which represents a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement from the fall that took it from $20.50 to $17.61," said Wee Woon Whai analyst at MMS in Hong Kong.
However, she said from here the next minor resistance level was at $19.40 a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement and then tougher resistance could be met at $19.71, the high of June 2.

Analysts said good supports were now in place to keep the market ranging higher but that it may have some difficulty breaking above $19.05 for a while with holidays in the U.S. slowing momentum though Wee Woon Whai said: "The holidays are fundamental. Technical factors are strong enough to push this market higher the weekend".

Analysts said the expanding triangle formation on the spot month continuation chart moving out between May 16s $20.60 high and the June 11 low of $17.32 continues to confirm the current trend while strong support around $18.50 as long as it is held continues to maintain bullish sentiment.

Gas oil held to a narrow range on Wednesday but opened and closed at the $167.50 a tonne forming a 'Doji at tops' candlestick on the spot month chart which flags uncertainty and indecision by buyers that will not maintain an uptrend.

However, analysts said the market was difficult to gauge at the moment with the narrow range unsurprising ahead of a holiday period though five-day RSI's are well into the 80 percent overbought region.
August Brent on SIMEX was trading at $18.90 per barrel, after London closed 12 cents higher at $18.92.
NYMEX was thinly traded, with August last traded at $20.28, down from six cents from the New York close where the contract had risen 22 cents to $20.34.
